stories.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
stories.summary: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used.
stories.why_it_matters: METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in ai & machine learning.
key_points: Problem & Context: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
Technical Implementation: METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans.
Deployment & Impact: Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete.

stories.summary: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Platforms Infrastructure Systems Physical Infrastructure Video Engineering & AR/VR Artificial Intelligence Watch Videos POSTED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2026 TO DEVINFRA, ML APPLICATIONS How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models By Rahul Suresh, Aayush Aggarwal, Aayush Prakash, Peggy Yao, Shiblee Sadik, Djordje Gligorijevic, Akshay Pardeshi, Yao Xuan, Anirudh Agrawal, Matan Levi, JP Owed, Anuj Bindal Our previous post in this series introduced the Ranking Engineer Agent (REA), an autonomous system that generates hypotheses, designs experiments, and proves new machine learning (ML) techniques on ads ranking models. stories.headline: Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem
stories.summary: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Open Source Meta Open Source Platforms Android iOS Web Infrastructure Systems Core Infra Data Infrastructure DevInfra Production Engineering Security & Privacy Research Publications Physical Infrastructure Connectivity Data Center Engineering Networking & Traffic Research Publications Video Engineering & AR/VR Video Engineering Virtual Reality Research Publications Artificial Intelligence ML Applications AI Research Research Publications Watch Videos POSTED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2026 TO DevInfra, ML Applications Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem By Anirudh Agrawal, Djordje Gligorijevic, Yao Xuan, Peggy Yao, Jiang Liu, John Martabano Landy, Rahul Suresh As ML ecosystems grow to a large number of production models, the bottleneck is no longer inventing new techniques to improve these models, but rather shipping them reliably and efficiently across a fragmented model space, creating a rising tide that lifts all the boats. At Meta, we built a template-driven approach that standardizes model design into a small set of reusable and composable building blocks, turning model iteration from a per-model problem into a shared systems problem.
stories.why_it_matters: Over the last two years, this approach reduced per-model engineering time by 92%, shipped 5000+ technique-model combinations, improved offline model quality by 0.63% on average at neutral serving capacity, and delivered 0.86% cumulative online lift covering 70% of models by count. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Skip to content Search this site Open Source Open Source Meta Open Source Platforms Android iOS Web Infrastructure Systems Core Infra Data Infrastructure DevInfra Production Engineering Security & Privacy Research Publications Physical Infrastructure Connectivity Data Center Engineering Networking & Traffic Research Publications Video Engineering & AR/VR Video Engineering Virtual Reality Research Publications Artificial Intelligence ML Applications AI Research Research Publications Watch Videos POSTED ON NOVEMBER 18, 2026 TO DevInfra, ML Applications Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem By Anirudh Agrawal, Djordje Gligorijevic, Yao Xuan, Peggy Yao, Jiang Liu, John Martabano Landy, Rahul Suresh As ML ecosystems grow to a large number of production models, the bottleneck is no longer inventing new techniques to improve these models, but rather shipping them reliably and efficiently across a fragmented model space, creating a rising tide that lifts all the boats.

Technical Implementation: At Meta, we built a template-driven approach that standardizes model design into a small set of reusable and composable building blocks, turning model iteration from a per-model problem into a shared systems problem.

Deployment & Impact: Over the last two years, this approach reduced per-model engineering time by 92%, shipped 5000+ technique-model combinations, improved offline model quality by 0.63% on average at neutral serving capacity, and delivered 0.86% cumulative online lift covering 70% of models by count.

stories.headline: Engineering AI Discover
stories.summary: The challenges and decisions behind AI Discover’s intelligence layer By Varun Khaitan , Peng Ren , Gary Tang , Itay Teller , Atif Faheem , Nipun Kumar , Donnie DeBoer , Eduardo Lundgren , Matteo Rinaldi , Raghav Bakshi We recently introduced AI Discover , a new tab in our TV app where a small group of members can try new ways to find something to watch. For years, our recommendations have worked in the background, inferring what a member might enjoy from their viewing history.
stories.why_it_matters: AI Discover moves from that silent ranking toward steerable discovery. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: Building AI Discover raised a question many teams will recognize: how do you deliver a better member experience with generative AI on TV without sacrificing speed, reliability or safety? Our answer is a new intelligence layer, the agent harness behind AI Discover.
Technical Implementation: For each request, it decides how to combine LLMs with our recommendation systems.
Deployment & Impact: It builds on years of work understanding what members enjoy, and on our recent work applying LLMs to recommendations and generative experiences.

stories.headline: Fact-Checking at Scale: Building a More Accurate and Efficient Synopsis Factuality System
stories.summary: By Shreya S Ramanujam , Yongce Li , Afshine Amidi , Sina Ghiassian , Benjamin Klein. Introduction Picture this — you’re home after a long day at work and can’t wait to catch up on Bridgerton.
stories.why_it_matters: You log on to Netflix, search for “Bridgerton” and land on this screen: If this sounds familiar, you already know what a synopsis is — it’s a short glimpse into what a viewer can expect to see in a show. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: At Netflix’s scale, with thousands of titles, multiple episodes per season and multiple languages, fact-checking all of these by hand simply doesn’t scale.

Technical Implementation: Our current factuality checker feeds a reasoning model everything we know about a title (like metadata and text assets) and asks it to judge synopsis factuality according to a rigorous rubric.

Deployment & Impact: There are two main limitations of this approach that we want to optimize: High cost of long-context reasoning calls: Each decision requires expensive, long-context model calls to reasoning models, which doesn’t scale well when we want to check multiple titles, episodes, languages, and style variants.
